newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain appeals for EU unity on political violence.
newsitem.headline: Spain appeals for EU unity on political violence.

text.p: Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said on Tuesday Spain and other countries that are the main targets of political violence should be able to set the tone for a unified European anti-terrorism strategy.
Mayor Oreja's assertion came after diplomatic clashes with Belgium and Portugal over their refusal to extradite suspected ETA Basque separatist guerrillas wanted by Spain.
"The countries which are victims are always right, not the observers," Mayor Oreja told reporters after meeting his French counterpart Jean-Louis Debre in Madrid.
Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, at a ceremony honouring Debre, called on 15 European Union nations to forge unified judicial, police and security policies.

Spain made similar appeals after the recent extradition disputes with its neighbours, calling on EU nations to ratify a treaty on extradition that Spanish authorities hope will make it easier to prosecute ETA suspects caught abroad.
Once the treaty is ratified, EU countries will no longer be able to refuse extradition of a suspect because the crime was politically motivated.

"It's absolutely fundamental to assure a common European space in police cooperation and security, to create a unified judicial space where questions such as asylum, extradition and security are treated in a common way by all members," Aznar said.

In two days of meetings, Debre and Mayor Oreja pledged to increase cooperation against ETA rebels, who have killed more than 800 people in a 29-year fight for an independent Basque state encompassing parts of southern France and northern Spain.
"We are united in the fight against Basque terrorism," Debre said on Tuesday.
On Monday night, he vowed France would aggressively pursue any leaders of ETA operating on French territory.
In the past, Madrid had complained the leadership of ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, used the Basque region of southern France as a haven to orchestrate attacks in Spain.
But Spain's 10-month-old conservative government has expressed its satisfaction with increasingly aggressive French action against ETA's network there.

Debre said under the terms of Europe's Schengen accords, Spanish police can operate against ETA in French terroritory but cannot detain suspects. Under those accords, seven EU countries agreed on a system of open borders and passport-free movement.
